The fibronectin-aggregacn (FAC) complex is a protein complex composed of fibronectin and aggrecan, which are key components of the extracellular matrix. It plays a crucial role in maintaining tissue structure, cell adhesion, and migration.

Research has shown that the FAC complex is present in injured cervical intervertebral disks. Biochemical analysis of such disks reveals the presence of inflammatory markers, including MCP (monocyte chemoattractant protein) and fragments of structural matrix proteins like aggrecan, as well as a correlation with pH. These findings suggest that the FAC complex may be involved in the pathogenesis of cervical disk disease.

Furthermore, studies have investigated the relationship between the FAC complex and spinal cord involvement in patients with cervical spondylotic amyotrophy (CSA). While not specifically looking at cervical disk disease, research indicates that signs of spinal cord involvement, such as a high signal intensity change on T2-weighted MRI and the pyramidal tract sign, can be associated with poor neurological prognosis.

In summary, the fibronectin-aggregacn complex is present in injured cervical intervertebral disks, and its presence may be linked to inflammation, matrix degradation, and spinal cord involvement. However, further research is needed to fully understand the role of the FAC complex in cervical disk disease and its implications for treatment and prognosis.
